holding_summary: A school-master's claim against a deceased ward's estate for the pupils' board and lodging is prescribed after one year, the same as an inn-keeper's claim for board and lodging, because by taking persons to board for hire the school-master assimilated himself to an inn-keeper for purposes of the prescription statute.

quotes.text: The claim of one whose occupation is that of a-school-master, for the hoard and lodging Of pupils, is prescribed by one year, under art. 3403 of the Civil Code.

court: Superior Court of the Territory of Orleans
holding_summary: The court held that the corporation of New Orleans, through rights inherited from the Spanish cabildo and confirmed by its 1805 charter, had authority to license and receive taxes on taverns, billiard-tables, and boarding-houses. It further held the city could require an applicant who in fact applied for and accepted a license covering all three cumulated objects to pay for the cumulated license, absent proof he had sought a license for a single object only.

quotes.text: I feel no difficulty, therefore in saying that the city may exact the tax from every tavern, billiard-table and boarding-house.

Whether they may cumulate two or the three taxes in one license, is a question which must surely be answered in the affirmative, in every case in which the applicant for a license desires it for the cumulated objects.

notes: Concerns municipal licensing/taxation of boarding-houses, taverns, and billiard-tables as businesses under the police power; does not classify an individual occupant's lodging arrangement, so characterization left null.
Concerns validity of a lease of riparian batture land for a coal/wood yard against a claim the river bank cannot be privately leased; no lodging or boarding-house facts.

holding_summary: A keeper of a boarding-house obtained arrest of a boarder and sequestration of his moveables and baggage for unpaid board and lodging on the ground he intended to remove from the state; the district court set the orders aside, finding no privilege as inn-keeper. The Supreme Court reversed, holding a boarder without a fixed domicile is subject to the boarding-house keeper's privilege as inn-keeper under Civil Code arts. 3200, 3202.

quotes.text: The plaintiff keeps a boarding-house in the city of New-Orleans, at which the defendant and his family lived as boarders.

Under the evidence, we consider that the property of the defendant is subject to the privilege of the-inn-keeper. The judgments of the District Court are, therefore, reversed, and the orders of arrest and sequestration are re-instated.

notes: Addresses the scope of an inn-keeper's liability as depositary for a traveler's stolen gold dust under Civil Code arts. 2936-2938; concerns tort/bailment liability for guest property, not the legal character or regulation of letting/lodging.

An overseer's occupancy of a plantation house is incident to his hiring as overseer, not a paid lodging arrangement; case addresses forcible removal of a discharged overseer, not letting for compensation.
